THESIS.md:
# Investment thesis — the Demo household

Agreed by Alex and Jordan. This is the policy; every money decision is
graded against it. Revisit at the monthly review, not mid-decision.

## What the money is for
- A house in ~3 years, Riley launched debt-free, and both of us optional-to-work by 60. Money buys calm, not stuff.

## Who you are (governs everything below)
- Two salaried W-2 incomes (Alex — product manager at BrightPath Labs; Jordan — teacher, Cedar Grove School District), one kid (Riley, 6). No equity comp, no debt beyond two credit cards paid monthly. Risk of drift, not disaster.

## The situation, said bluntly
- Savings are healthy but unexamined: cash piles up in checking and nobody has audited the recurring charges in years. The portfolio is fine; the plumbing has never been checked for leaks.

## Standing rules
- New money: 529 first ($300/mo), then the house fund (HYSA), then taxable index funds. No individual stocks, no leverage, no options. Cards on autopay, paid in full, every month.

## Risk posture
- 80/20 equities/bonds in retirement accounts. A 30% drawdown changes nothing; the house timeline flexes before the allocation does.

## Cash cushion
- Six months of baseline spend (~$40k) stays in the Ally HYSA. The house fund grows on top of that, never instead of it.

## Spending
- ~$6.5k/mo baseline. No line-item policing — flag recurring waste and drift over 15%, not lattes.

## How we work together
- Monthly 15-minute review. Be blunt, propose the number, one open item at a time. Both adults sign off on anything irreversible.

## Goal targets
- House: $120k down payment fund by 2029. 529: $120k for Riley by 2038. Retirement: $2M invested by 2055.
